## Restrict Python script export option to Python notebooks

The export quick-pick menu currently offers "Export As Python Script" for all notebook types, even when the notebook's metadata indicates a non-Python kernel. This is misleading and can result in attempting to convert unsupported notebook formats to Python. We need to ensure the Python export option is only presented when the notebook's language is Python, while keeping HTML and PDF export options available for all notebook types.

293: function createNotebookCellDataFromCodeCell(
294:     isNbTrusted: boolean,
295:     cell: nbformat.ICodeCell,
296:     cellLanguage: string
297: ): NotebookCellData {
298:     // tslint:disable-next-line: no-any
299:     const cellOutputs: nbformat.IOutput[] = Array.isArray(cell.outputs) ? cell.outputs : [];
300:     const outputs = createVSCCellOutputsFromOutputs(cellOutputs);
301:     // If we have an execution count & no errors, then success state.
302:     // If we have an execution count &  errors, then error state.
303:     // Else idle state.
304:     const hasErrors = outputs.some((output) => output.outputKind === vscodeNotebookEnums.CellOutputKind.Error);
305:     const hasExecutionCount = typeof cell.execution_count === 'number' && cell.execution_count > 0;
306:     let runState: NotebookCellRunState;
307:     let statusMessage: string | undefined;
308:     if (!hasExecutionCount) {
309:         runState = vscodeNotebookEnums.NotebookCellRunState.Idle;
310:     } else if (hasErrors) {
311:         runState = vscodeNotebookEnums.NotebookCellRunState.Error;
312:         // Error details are stripped from the output, get raw output.
313:         // tslint:disable-next-line: no-any
314:         statusMessage = getCellStatusMessageBasedOnFirstErrorOutput(cellOutputs);
315:     } else {
316:         runState = vscodeNotebookEnums.NotebookCellRunState.Success;
317:     }
318: 
319:     const vscodeMetadata = (cell.metadata.vscode as unknown) as IBaseCellVSCodeMetadata | undefined;
320:     const startExecutionTime = vscodeMetadata?.start_execution_time
321:         ? new Date(Date.parse(vscodeMetadata.start_execution_time)).getTime()
322:         : undefined;
323:     const endExecutionTime = vscodeMetadata?.end_execution_time
324:         ? new Date(Date.parse(vscodeMetadata.end_execution_time)).getTime()
325:         : undefined;
326: 
327:     let runStartTime: undefined | number;
328:     let lastRunDuration: undefined | number;
329:     if (startExecutionTime && typeof endExecutionTime === 'number') {
330:         runStartTime = startExecutionTime;
331:         lastRunDuration = endExecutionTime - startExecutionTime;
332:     }
333: 
334:     const notebookCellMetadata: NotebookCellMetadata = {
335:         editable: isNbTrusted,
336:         executionOrder: typeof cell.execution_count === 'number' ? cell.execution_count : undefined,
337:         hasExecutionOrder: true,
338:         runState,
339:         runnable: isNbTrusted,
340:         statusMessage,
341:         runStartTime,
342:         lastRunDuration,
343:         custom: getCustomNotebookCellMetadata(cell)
344:     };
345: 
346:     // If not trusted, then clear the output in VSC Cell (for untrusted notebooks we do not display output).
347:     // At this point we have the original output in the ICell.
348:     if (!isNbTrusted) {
349:         while (outputs.length) {
350:             outputs.shift();
351:         }
352:     }
353: 
354:     const source = concatMultilineString(cell.source);
355: 
356:     return {
357:         cellKind: vscodeNotebookEnums.CellKind.Code,
358:         language: cellLanguage,
359:         metadata: notebookCellMetadata,
360:         source,
361:         outputs
362:     };
363: }

375:                     return;
376:                 default:
377:                     return;
378:             }
379:         })
380:         .filter((output) => !!output)
381:         .map((output) => output!!);

486: const cellOutputMappers = new Map<
487:     nbformat.OutputType,
488:     (output: nbformat.IOutput, outputType: nbformat.OutputType) => CellOutput
489: >();
490: // tslint:disable-next-line: no-any
491: cellOutputMappers.set('display_data', translateDisplayDataOutput as any);
492: // tslint:disable-next-line: no-any
493: cellOutputMappers.set('error', translateErrorOutput as any);
494: // tslint:disable-next-line: no-any
495: cellOutputMappers.set('execute_result', translateDisplayDataOutput as any);
496: // tslint:disable-next-line: no-any
497: cellOutputMappers.set('stream', translateStreamOutput as any);
498: // tslint:disable-next-line: no-any
499: cellOutputMappers.set('update_display_data', translateDisplayDataOutput as any);
500: export function cellOutputToVSCCellOutput(output: nbformat.IOutput): CellOutput {
501:     const fn = cellOutputMappers.get(output.output_type as nbformat.OutputType);
502:     let result: CellOutput;
503:     if (fn) {
504:         result = fn(output, (output.output_type as unknown) as nbformat.OutputType);
505:     } else {
506:         traceWarning(`Unable to translate cell from ${output.output_type} to NotebookCellData for VS Code.`);
507:         result = {
508:             outputKind: vscodeNotebookEnums.CellOutputKind.Rich,
509:             // tslint:disable-next-line: no-any
510:             data: output.data as any,
511:             metadata: { custom: { vscode: { outputType: output.output_type } } }
512:         };
513:     }
514: 
515:     // Add on transient data if we have any. This should be removed by our save functions elsewhere.
516:     if (
517:         output.transient &&
518:         result &&
519:         result.outputKind === vscodeNotebookEnums.CellOutputKind.Rich &&
520:         result.metadata
521:     ) {
522:         // tslint:disable-next-line: no-any
523:         result.metadata.custom = { ...result.metadata.custom, transient: output.transient };
524:     }
525:     return result;
526: }

546: /**
547:  * Converts a Jupyter display cell output into a VSCode cell output format.
548:  * Handles sizing, adding backgrounds to images and the like.
549:  * E.g. Jupyter cell output contains metadata to add backgrounds to images, here we generate the necessary HTML.
550:  *
551:  * @export
552:  * @param {nbformat.IDisplayData} output
553:  * @returns {(CellDisplayOutput | undefined)}
554:  */
555: function translateDisplayDataOutput(
556:     output: nbformat.IDisplayData | nbformat.IDisplayUpdate | nbformat.IExecuteResult,
557:     outputType: nbformat.OutputType
558: ): CellDisplayOutput | undefined {
559:     const data = { ...output.data };
560:     // tslint:disable-next-line: no-any
561:     const metadata = output.metadata ? ({ custom: cloneDeep(output.metadata) } as any) : { custom: {} };
562:     metadata.custom.vscode = { outputType };
563:     if (output.execution_count) {
564:         metadata.custom.vscode.execution_count = output.execution_count;
565:     }
566:     return {
567:         outputKind: vscodeNotebookEnums.CellOutputKind.Rich,
568:         data,
569:         metadata // Used be renderers & VS Code for diffing (it knows what has changed).
570:     };
571: }

573: function translateStreamOutput(output: nbformat.IStream, outputType: nbformat.OutputType): CellDisplayOutput {
574:     // Do not return as `CellOutputKind.Text`. VSC will not translate ascii output correctly.

576:     return {
577:         outputKind: vscodeNotebookEnums.CellOutputKind.Rich,
578:         data: {
579:             ['text/plain']: concatMultilineString(output.text, true)
580:         },
581:         metadata: {
582:             custom: { vscode: { outputType, name: output.name } }
583:         }

587: export function isStreamOutput(output: CellOutput, expectedStreamName: string): boolean {
588:     if (output.outputKind !== vscodeNotebookEnums.CellOutputKind.Rich) {
589:         return false;

591:     output = (output as unknown) as CellDisplayOutput;
592:     if (!('text/plain' in output.data)) {
593:         return false;
594:     }
595:     // Logic of metadata can be found here translateStreamOutput.
596:     // That function adds the vscode metadata.
597:     if (output.metadata?.custom?.vscode?.outputType !== 'stream') {
598:         return false;
599:     }
600:     if (expectedStreamName && output.metadata?.custom?.vscode?.name !== expectedStreamName) {
601:         return false;
602:     }
603:     return true;
604: }

615: type JupyterOutput =
616:     | nbformat.IUnrecognizedOutput
617:     | nbformat.IExecuteResult
618:     | nbformat.IDisplayData
619:     | nbformat.IStream
620:     | nbformat.IError;

622: function translateCellDisplayOutput(output: CellDisplayOutput): JupyterOutput {
623:     const outputType: nbformat.OutputType = output.metadata?.custom?.vscode?.outputType;
624:     let result: JupyterOutput;
625:     switch (outputType) {
626:         case 'stream':
627:             {
628:                 result = {
629:                     output_type: 'stream',
630:                     name: output.metadata?.custom?.vscode?.name,
631:                     text: splitMultilineString(output.data['text/plain'])
632:                 };
633:             }
634:             break;
635:         case 'display_data':
636:             {
637:                 const metadata = getSanitizedCellMetadata(output.metadata?.custom);
638:                 result = {
639:                     output_type: 'display_data',
640:                     data: output.data,
641:                     metadata
642:                 };
643:             }
644:             break;
645:         case 'execute_result':
646:             {
647:                 const metadata = getSanitizedCellMetadata(output.metadata?.custom);
648:                 result = {
649:                     output_type: 'execute_result',
650:                     data: output.data,
651:                     metadata,
652:                     execution_count: output.metadata?.custom?.vscode?.execution_count
653:                 };
654:             }
655:             break;
656:         case 'update_display_data':
657:             {
658:                 const metadata = getSanitizedCellMetadata(output.metadata?.custom);
659:                 result = {
660:                     output_type: 'update_display_data',
661:                     data: output.data,
662:                     metadata
663:                 };
664:             }
665:             break;
666:         default:
667:             {
668:                 sendTelemetryEvent(Telemetry.VSCNotebookCellTranslationFailed, undefined, {
669:                     isErrorOutput: outputType === 'error'
670:                 });
671:                 const metadata = getSanitizedCellMetadata(output.metadata?.custom);
672:                 const unknownOutput: nbformat.IUnrecognizedOutput = { output_type: outputType };
673:                 if (Object.keys(metadata).length > 0) {
674:                     unknownOutput.metadata = metadata;
675:                 }
676:                 if (Object.keys(output.data).length > 0) {

1: # News
2: 
3: Our changelog is automatically generated from individual news entry files.
4: This alleviates the burden of having to go back and try to figure out
5: what changed in a release. It also helps tie pull requests back to the
6: issue(s) it addresses. Finally, it avoids merge conflicts between pull requests
7: which would occur if multiple pull requests tried to edit the changelog.
8: 
9: If a change does not warrant a news entry, the `skip news` label can be added
10: to a pull request to signal this fact.
11: 
12: ## Entries
13: 
14: Each news entry is represented by a Markdown file that contains the
15: relevant details of what changed. The file name of the news entry is
16: the issue that corresponds to the change along with an optional nonce in
17: case a single issue corresponds to multiple changes. The directory
18: the news entry is saved in specifies what section of the changelog the
19: change corresponds to. External contributors should also make sure to
20: thank themselves for taking the time and effort to contribute.
21: 
22: As an example, a change corresponding to a bug reported in issue #42
23: would be saved in the `1 Fixes` directory and named `42.md`
24: (or `42-nonce_value.md` if there was a need for multiple entries
25: regarding issue #42) and could contain the following:
26: 
27: ```markdown
28: [Answer](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/42_(number)>)
29: to the Ultimate Question of Life, the Universe, and Everything!
30: (thanks [Don Jaymanne](https://github.com/donjayamanne/))
31: ```
32: 
33: This would then be made into an entry in the changelog that was in the
34: `Fixes` section, contained the details as found in the file, and tied
35: to issue #42.
36: 
37: ## Generating the changelog
38: 
39: The `announce` script can do 3 possible things:
40: 
41: 1. Validate that the changelog _could_ be successfully generated
42: 2. Generate the changelog entries
43: 3. Generate the changelog entries **and** `git-rm` the news entry files
44: 
45: The first option is used in CI to make sure any added news entries
46: will not cause trouble at release time. The second option is for
47: filling in the changelog for interim releases, e.g. a beta release.
48: The third option is for final releases that get published to the
49: [VS Code marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/VSCode).
50: 
51: For options 2 & 3, the changelog is sent to stdout so it can be temporarily
52: saved to a file:
53: 
54: ```sh
55: python3 news > entry.txt
56: ```
57: 
58: It can also be redirected to an editor buffer, e.g.:
59: 
60: ```sh
61: python3 news | code-insiders -
62: ```

We need to re-introduce a survey prompt specifically for users on the Insiders build who are working with native notebooks. The goal is to gather feedback from this cohort without disturbing stable-channel users.

    Currently, the existing data science survey banner is shown to all users (except on Web UI). We want to:
    - Show the existing data science survey only on the **stable** channel.
    - Add a new, separate survey banner for **Insiders** users that targets the native notebooks experience (triggered by notebook open/execution thresholds).
    - Ensure only one survey prompt can appear at a time — the stable survey for stable users, and the Insiders notebooks survey for Insiders users.

    Additionally, when a user dismisses the survey (chooses "No, thanks"), we should not permanently suppress it; instead, re-prompt after a cooldown period (3 months for "No", 6 months after taking the survey). The survey banner should also be registered and wired into the service registry so it is activated with the extension.

## Environment Setup
Check `package.json` at the repo root for the project's npm scripts and dependencies. Look at `src/client/common/types.ts`, `src/client/activation/serviceRegistry.ts`, `src/client/datascience/dataScienceSurveyBanner.ts`, and `src/client/common/utils/localize.ts` to understand the existing banner architecture. Test configuration for unit tests is in `build/.mocha.unittests.ts.json` and `build/.mocha.unittests.json` — refer to those for how tests are run. Also see `CONTRIBUTING.md` for general dev setup guidance.

## Implementation Plan
1. **Add a new banner name constant** in `src/client/common/types.ts`:
       - Add `BANNER_NAME_INSIDERS_NOTEBOOKS_SURVEY = 'DSInsidersNotebooksSurvey'`.
       - Remove the `enabled` property from the `IJupyterExtensionBanner` interface (or keep it internal to each implementer, not part of the public interface) so each banner can independently decide its gating conditions.

    2. **Create a new survey banner class** at `src/client/datascience/insidersNativeNotebookSurveyBanner.ts`:
       - Implement `IJupyterExtensionBanner`.
       - Gate visibility on:
         - User is on the **Insiders** channel (via `IApplicationEnvironment.channel`).
         - Not on Web UI (`env.uiKind !== UIKind.Web`).
         - The user is in the native notebooks experiment (using `IExperimentService.inExperiment`).
         - Usage thresholds: opened more than 5 notebooks OR executed more than 100 cells (track in persistent state using `IPersistentStateFactory`).
       - Use the `InsidersNativeNotebooksSurveyBanner` localization namespace (to be added in `localize.ts`).
       - On "Yes": launch the survey URL (`https://aka.ms/vscjupyternb`) and disable for 6 months.
       - On "No": disable for 3 months.
       - On dismiss: disable for the current session only.
       - The `disable(months: number)` method should store a global state with an expiry duration (use `IPersistentStateFactory.createGlobalPersistentState` with `expiryDurationMs`).

    3. **Update `src/client/datascience/dataScienceSurveyBanner.ts`**:
       - Inject `IApplicationEnvironment` and add a new constructor parameter (or use the existing one) to read the extension channel.
       - Change the `enabled` getter to also require `this.applicationEnvironment.channel === 'stable'` (so it only shows on stable builds).
       - Update `showBanner` to call `disable(6)` for "Yes" and `disable(3)` for "No" (instead of permanent disable).
       - Update `disable()` to accept a months parameter and pass it to `createGlobalPersistentState` with an expiry duration.

    4. **Update `DataScienceSurveyBannerLogger`** (used for tracking interactive window executions):
       - Inject both the existing `BANNER_NAME_DS_SURVEY` and the new `BANNER_NAME_INSIDERS_NOTEBOOKS_SURVEY` banners.
       - When execution counts are updated, call `showBanner()` on **both** banners via `Promise.all`.

    5. **Register the new banner** in `src/client/activation/serviceRegistry.ts`:
       - Import the new `InsidersNativeNotebooksSurveyBanner` and the new constant.
       - Add a new `serviceManager.addSingleton<IJupyterExtensionBanner>(IJupyterExtensionBanner, InsidersNativeNotebooksSurveyBanner, BANNER_NAME_INSIDERS_NOTEBOOKS_SURVEY)` call.

    6. **Add a localization namespace** in `src/client/common/utils/localize.ts`:
       - Add `InsidersNativeNotebooksSurveyBanner` namespace with `bannerMessage` = `'Can you please take a minute to tell us about your notebooks experience in VS Code?'`.
       - Reuse the `bannerLabelYes` / `bannerLabelNo` from the `DataScienceSurveyBanner` namespace.

    7. **Update existing unit tests** for the data science banner in `src/test/datascience/datascienceSurveyBanner.unit.test.ts`:
       - Modify the test helper `preparePopup` to accept a `channel` parameter (`'stable'` or `'insiders'`) and mock `IApplicationEnvironment`.
       - Add a test confirming the data science banner does **not** show when the channel is `'insiders'`.

    8. **Create new unit tests** in `src/test/datascience/insidersNativeNotebookSurveyBanner.unit.test.ts`:
       - Test that the banner shows when:
         - Channel is `insiders`, experiment is enabled, and execution count >= 100.
         - Channel is `insiders`, experiment is enabled, and notebook open count > 5.
       - Test that the banner does **not** show when:
         - Channel is `stable`.
         - The experiment flag is off.
         - The banner is disabled in persistent state.
         - Usage thresholds are not met.
       - Test the survey launch uses the correct URL.

54:         const optOutFrom = this.settings.experiments.optOutFrom;
55:         this._optInto = optInto.filter((exp) => !exp.endsWith('control'));
56:         this._optOutFrom = optOutFrom.filter((exp) => !exp.endsWith('control'));

58:         // Don't initialize the experiment service if the extension's experiments setting is disabled.

70:         }

11:     constructor(
12:         private storage: Memento,
13:         private key: string,
14:         private defaultValue?: T,
15:         private expiryDurationMs?: number
16:     ) {}

18:     public get value(): T {
19:         if (this.expiryDurationMs) {
20:             const cachedData = this.storage.get<{ data?: T; expiry?: number }>(this.key, { data: this.defaultValue! });
21:             if (!cachedData || !cachedData.expiry || cachedData.expiry < Date.now()) {
22:                 return this.defaultValue!;
23:             } else {
24:                 return cachedData.data!;
25:             }
26:         } else {
27:             return this.storage.get<T>(this.key, this.defaultValue!);
28:         }
29:     }
30: 
31:     public async updateValue(newValue: T): Promise<void> {
32:         if (this.expiryDurationMs) {
33:             await this.storage.update(this.key, { data: newValue, expiry: Date.now() + this.expiryDurationMs });
34:         } else {
35:             await this.storage.update(this.key, newValue);
36:         }
37:     }
38: }

1: # News
2: 
3: Our changelog is automatically generated from individual news entry files.
4: This alleviates the burden of having to go back and try to figure out
5: what changed in a release. It also helps tie pull requests back to the
6: issue(s) it addresses. Finally, it avoids merge conflicts between pull requests
7: which would occur if multiple pull requests tried to edit the changelog.
8: 
9: If a change does not warrant a news entry, the `skip news` label can be added
10: to a pull request to signal this fact.
11: 
12: ## Entries
13: 
14: Each news entry is represented by a Markdown file that contains the
15: relevant details of what changed. The file name of the news entry is
16: the issue that corresponds to the change along with an optional nonce in
17: case a single issue corresponds to multiple changes. The directory
18: the news entry is saved in specifies what section of the changelog the
19: change corresponds to. External contributors should also make sure to
20: thank themselves for taking the time and effort to contribute.
21: 
22: As an example, a change corresponding to a bug reported in issue #42
23: would be saved in the `1 Fixes` directory and named `42.md`
24: (or `42-nonce_value.md` if there was a need for multiple entries
25: regarding issue #42) and could contain the following:
26: 
27: ```markdown
28: [Answer](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/42_(number)>)
29: to the Ultimate Question of Life, the Universe, and Everything!
30: (thanks [Don Jaymanne](https://github.com/donjayamanne/))
31: ```
32: 
33: This would then be made into an entry in the changelog that was in the
34: `Fixes` section, contained the details as found in the file, and tied
35: to issue #42.
36: 
37: ## Generating the changelog
38: 
39: The `announce` script can do 3 possible things:
40: 
41: 1. Validate that the changelog _could_ be successfully generated
42: 2. Generate the changelog entries
43: 3. Generate the changelog entries **and** `git-rm` the news entry files
44: 
45: The first option is used in CI to make sure any added news entries
46: will not cause trouble at release time. The second option is for
47: filling in the changelog for interim releases, e.g. a beta release.
48: The third option is for final releases that get published to the
49: [VS Code marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/VSCode).
50: 
51: For options 2 & 3, the changelog is sent to stdout so it can be temporarily
52: saved to a file:
53: 
54: ```sh
55: python3 news > entry.txt
56: ```
57: 
58: It can also be redirected to an editor buffer, e.g.:
59: 
60: ```sh
61: python3 news | code-insiders -
62: ```

Implement a one-time migration that rewrites all `python.dataScience.*` settings in `settings.json` files and keyboard bindings in `keybindings.json` to their new `jupyter.*` equivalents. This is needed because the Data Science functionality has been extracted from the Python extension into a separate Jupyter extension, so all configuration keys are being namespaced under `jupyter.` going forward.

    The migration must:
    - Run once per user (tracked via persistent global state) to avoid slower activation on every startup.
    - Handle the special case of `python.dataScience.jupyterServerURI`: its value is moved to server URI storage, and the setting is rewritten as `jupyter.jupyterServerType` with a value of either `local` or `remote`.
    - Avoid overwriting settings or keybindings that the user has already defined under the new `jupyter.` namespace.
    - Gracefully handle missing files (e.g., `keybindings.json` may not exist) and malformed JSONC content.

## Environment Setup
- Check `package.json` for the main `npm` scripts used to build, lint, and run unit tests.
    - Look at `build/.mocha.unittests.ts.json` and `build/.mocha.unittests.js.json` for how unit test suites are configured and targeted.
    - For Python-side tooling (if relevant), refer to `pythonFiles/pyproject.toml`.
    - Check `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `CODING_STANDARDS.md` for project conventions.

## Implementation Plan
1. Update `src/client/common/application/types.ts`:
       - Add a readonly property `userCustomKeybindingsFile: string | undefined` to the `IApplicationEnvironment` interface, with a doc comment noting the file may or may not exist.

    2. Update `src/client/common/application/applicationEnvironment.ts`:
       - Inject `IExtensionContext` into the `ApplicationEnvironment` constructor (from `../types`).
       - Implement `get userCustomKeybindingsFile()` to return `path.resolve(path.join(this.extensionContext.globalStoragePath, '..', '..', 'keybindings.json'))`.
       - Update the constructor parameter list and the `extension-version.functional.test.ts` construction accordingly.

    3. Update `src/client/activation/migrateDataScienceSettingsService.ts`:
       - Inject `IPersistentStateFactory` into the constructor.
       - In `activate()`, check a global persistent state flag (e.g., key `'MigratedDataScienceSettingsService'`, default `false`). Only run the migration when the flag is `false`, and set it to `true` after a successful run (use `.ignoreErrors()` on the update).
       - Split the existing `fixSettingInFile` into a private `fixSettingsFile(filePath)` that also handles `keybindings.json` (passed in from `updateSettings`). Consider adding a parameter or separate method for keybindings since the key structure is different (array of `{ key, command, when? }` objects).
       - In `fixSettingsFile`:
         - Read the file; if it does not contain `python.dataScience`, return early.
         - Parse with `jsonc-parser`; on parse errors, log and return.
         - Collect keys that start with `python.dataScience` (use `startsWith`, not `includes`).
         - For each key:
           - Remove the old key from the file contents.
           - Compute the new key as `jupyter.${k.substr(19)}`.
           - For `python.dataScience.jupyterServerURI`: call `serverUriStorage.setUri(val)`, set `newKey = 'jupyter.jupyterServerType'`, and set `val` to `Settings.JupyterServerLocalLaunch` or `Settings.JupyterServerRemoteLaunch` (based on whether the original value equals `Settings.JupyterServerLocalLaunch`).
           - If the target key already exists in the parsed content (case-sensitive), skip adding the new key to avoid duplicates.
         - Write the modified contents back with `fs.writeLocalFile`.
       - Update `updateSettings(resource)` to also include `this.application.userCustomKeybindingsFile` in the list of files to process.
       - Update `getSettingsFiles` and `getFilesToBeFixed` to handle the keybindings file (it may not exist; use `localFileExists` and skip if missing).

    4. Update `src/test/datascience/mockFileSystem.ts`:
       - Override `localFileExists(filePath)` to first check the in-memory `contentOverloads` map, falling back to `super.localFileExists` when not found.

    5. Rewrite `src/test/activation/migrateDataScienceSettingsService.unit.test.ts`:
       - Mock `IPersistentStateFactory` and a `PersistentState` instance that returns `false` initially.
       - Use `fullMigrationTest` (or similar) that exercises the public `activate()` method (rather than the now-private internals) and verifies the settings file is rewritten correctly.
       - Add a test that verifies the migration runs only once (second `activate()` call does not rewrite).
       - Add a test that verifies `jupyter.jupyterServerType` is not duplicated when it already exists.
       - Add a test for `keybindings.json` migration when the file exists.

    6. Add a news entry file under `news/2 Fixes/1088.md` describing the migration for users.

1: # News
2: 
3: Our changelog is automatically generated from individual news entry files.
4: This alleviates the burden of having to go back and try to figure out
5: what changed in a release. It also helps tie pull requests back to the
6: issue(s) it addresses. Finally, it avoids merge conflicts between pull requests
7: which would occur if multiple pull requests tried to edit the changelog.
8: 
9: If a change does not warrant a news entry, the `skip news` label can be added
10: to a pull request to signal this fact.
11: 
12: ## Entries
13: 
14: Each news entry is represented by a Markdown file that contains the
15: relevant details of what changed. The file name of the news entry is
16: the issue that corresponds to the change along with an optional nonce in
17: case a single issue corresponds to multiple changes. The directory
18: the news entry is saved in specifies what section of the changelog the
19: change corresponds to. External contributors should also make sure to
20: thank themselves for taking the time and effort to contribute.
21: 
22: As an example, a change corresponding to a bug reported in issue #42
23: would be saved in the `1 Fixes` directory and named `42.md`
24: (or `42-nonce_value.md` if there was a need for multiple entries
25: regarding issue #42) and could contain the following:
26: 
27: ```markdown
28: [Answer](<https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/42_(number)>)
29: to the Ultimate Question of Life, the Universe, and Everything!
30: (thanks [Don Jaymanne](https://github.com/donjayamanne/))
31: ```
32: 
33: This would then be made into an entry in the changelog that was in the
34: `Fixes` section, contained the details as found in the file, and tied
35: to issue #42.
36: 
37: ## Generating the changelog
38: 
39: The `announce` script can do 3 possible things:
40: 
41: 1. Validate that the changelog _could_ be successfully generated
42: 2. Generate the changelog entries
43: 3. Generate the changelog entries **and** `git-rm` the news entry files
44: 
45: The first option is used in CI to make sure any added news entries
46: will not cause trouble at release time. The second option is for
47: filling in the changelog for interim releases, e.g. a beta release.
48: The third option is for final releases that get published to the
49: [VS Code marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/VSCode).
50: 
51: For options 2 & 3, the changelog is sent to stdout so it can be temporarily
52: saved to a file:
53: 
54: ```sh
55: python3 news > entry.txt
56: ```
57: 
58: It can also be redirected to an editor buffer, e.g.:
59: 
60: ```sh
61: python3 news | code-insiders -
62: ```

We need to enhance the kernel spec model and the raw kernel implementation to support long-running kernel workflows. Specifically:

    1. The `IJupyterKernelSpec` interface and `JupyterKernelSpec` class should expose the `interrupt_mode` field that can be part of a kernel spec. This field indicates whether a kernel should be interrupted via a message or a signal, and will be needed by higher-level components when they decide how to interrupt a kernel.

    2. The `RawKernel.getSpec()` method currently delegates directly to the underlying JupyterLab kernel, which may fail or behave incorrectly when working with local kernel processes. We need to improve this method so that, when the kernel comes from a local kernel spec, we return the kernel spec data directly from our internal kernel connection metadata instead of relying on the JupyterLab API. This avoids unnecessary round-trips and potential failures.

    This is foundational work — it doesn't fix a user-facing bug yet, but it adds the data and behavior we'll need for upcoming long-running kernel support.

## Environment Setup
Check the following repo files for build, install, and test setup:
    - `package.json` — main Node.js project configuration and scripts
    - `tsconfig.json`, `tsconfig.extension.json` — TypeScript build configuration
    - `.eslintrc`, `tslint.json` — linting configuration
    - `build/.mocha.unittests.json`, `build/.mocha.unittests.js.json`, `build/.mocha.unittests.ts.json` — unit test mocha configurations
    - `pythonFiles/pyproject.toml` — Python-side dependency configuration if needed

## Implementation Plan
1. Add `interrupt_mode` to the `IJupyterKernelSpec` interface in `src/client/datascience/types.ts`
       - Add a new optional property: `readonly interrupt_mode?: 'message' | 'signal';`
       - Place it near the other kernel spec metadata fields (e.g., after `interpreterPath`)

    2. Update the `JupyterKernelSpec` class in `src/client/datascience/jupyter/kernels/jupyterKernelSpec.ts`:
       - Add a public property: `public interrupt_mode?: 'message' | 'signal';`
       - In the constructor, copy the `interrupt_mode` value from `specModel.interrupt_mode` (use a cast if needed since `Kernel.ISpecModel` may type it as `any`)

    3. Update the `RawKernel.getSpec()` method in `src/client/datascience/raw-kernel/rawKernel.ts`:
       - Change the method from synchronous return to `async` method

       - Return an object spreading the kernel spec plus the `resources` property
       - If not using a kernel spec, log an error indicating we're falling back to JLab API and return `this.realKernel.getSpec()`

237: export function createRawKernel(kernelProcess: IKernelProcess, clientId: string): RawKernel {
238:     const jupyterLab = require('@jupyterlab/services') as typeof import('@jupyterlab/services'); // NOSONAR
239:     const jupyterLabSerialize = require('@jupyterlab/services/lib/kernel/serialize') as typeof import('@jupyterlab/services/lib/kernel/serialize'); // NOSONAR
240: 
241:     // Dummy websocket we give to the underlying real kernel
242:     let socketInstance: any;
243:     class RawSocketWrapper extends RawSocket {
244:         constructor() {
245:             super(kernelProcess.connection, jupyterLabSerialize.serialize, jupyterLabSerialize.deserialize);
246:             socketInstance = this;
247:         }
248:     }
249: 
250:     // Remap the server settings for the real kernel to use our dummy websocket
251:     const settings = jupyterLab.ServerConnection.makeSettings({
252:         WebSocket: RawSocketWrapper as any, // NOSONAR
253:         wsUrl: 'RAW'
254:     });
255: 
256:     // Then create the real kernel. We will remap its serialize/deserialize functions
257:     // to do nothing so that we can control serialization at our socket layer.
258:     if (!nonSerializingKernel) {
259:         // Note, this is done with a postInstall step (found in build\ci\postInstall.js). In that post install step
260:         // we eliminate the serialize import from the default kernel and remap it to do nothing.
261:         nonSerializingKernel = require('@jupyterlab/services/lib/kernel/nonSerializingKernel') as typeof import('@jupyterlab/services/lib/kernel/default'); // NOSONAR
262:     }
263:     const realKernel = new nonSerializingKernel.DefaultKernel(
264:         {
265:             name: getNameOfKernelConnection(kernelProcess.kernelConnectionMetadata),
266:             serverSettings: settings,
267:             clientId,
268:             handleComms: true
269:         },
270:         uuid()
271:     );
272: 
273:     // Use this real kernel in result.
274:     return new RawKernel(realKernel, socketInstance, kernelProcess);
